tables.caption: Coat of arms of City of Brussels
headers: Coronet A Belgian Count 's coronet Escutcheon Gules Saint Michael Or, slaying the Devil Sable Supporters Two lions rampant Or armed and langued Gules each holding a banner: dexter, the arms of the Duchy of Brabant, also those of Belgium, sinister, the city's arms Compartment A mount vert Symbolism Saint Michael is the city's patron saint. [ 27 ] See: Saint Michael slaying the Devil Previous versions See below

rows: The Original arms were plain Gules. [ 28 ] From the 16th century on, it was customary to put the figure of the city seal representing Saint Michael, first as a shadow then in a more elaborate form. [ 29 ] Note: many of the arms of the Seven Noble Houses of Brussels were variants of these arms.
